- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 75% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below 70%, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “volatility dampener” — reduce first 5 days’ forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
